indicators.ind: L1- Proportion of households using basic drinking water services
indicators.mov: CV003 - Baseline and end project evaluation report

itt.stmt: Improved WASH behaviors through behavior change programs and appropriate WASH infrastructure at the community level.
itt.ind: L1- Proportion of households using basic drinking water services
itt.defn:
Proportion of the households using an improved drinking water source within 30 minutes round trip of their household, including queuing time. 
An improved drinking water source:, by nature of its construction or through active intervention, is likely to be protected from outside contamination, in particular from contamination with faecal matter and more likely to provide "safe" water, such as a household connection, a borehole, etc.
This indicator measures the proportion of households with access to a basic drinking water supply. A basic drinking water facility is defined as an improved water source within 30 minute round trip of household, including queuing time, including water sources on plot.
An improved drinking water facility is defined as a source or delivery point that by nature of its construction, or through active intervention, is protected from outside contamination, in particular from contamination with fecal matter. The following are considered to be improved drinking water facilities: piped drinking water supply on premises; public taps/stand posts; tube well/ borehole; protected dug well; protected spring; rainwater. Packaged water is considered improved if households use an improved water facility for other domestic purposes.
When measuring this indicator over time, ensure that it is measured in the same seasons to account for fluctuations in seasonality. If not possible, ask questions for wet and dry season availability to better understand seasonal changes.

**This indicator is measured under Annual Impact Measurement (AIM)**
itt.mov: CV003 - Baseline and end project evaluation report

itt.defn:
Number of people gaining access to improved sanitation facilities which are not shared with other households. Key definitions in the regard are:
-- Improved sanitation facilities: Those that effectively separate excreta from human contact and ensure that excreta do not reenter the immediate household environment. -- Gaining access: Access to a basic sanitation service occurs or is gained when the sanitation facility is (1) newly established; (2) upgraded from an unimproved facility; or (3) rehabilitated from a non-functional state (after a minimum period of 12 months of not functioning). Households counted under this indicator must not have already had similar "access", meaning that a nonshared, improved sanitation facility was not available for household use prior to completion of the facility attributed to World Vision sanitation programming. Count only facilities completed during the reporting period as a result of World Vision programming.

Number of targeted households that adopt context-appropriate point-of-use (POU) water treatment technologies during the reporting period as a result of World Vision programming. Such POU technologies may include P&G packets, chlorine-based products, flocculation chemicals, water filters, and the like. Key terms are defined as follows:
-- Targeted households: Those households that participated in a World Vision household water treatment and safe storage (HWTS) training;  
-- Adopt: The adoption of a treatment technology is measured through direct observation at the household where the data collector confirms the presence of the technology and evidence that it is currently being used. Please see the "how to measure" section for specific guidelines for household observations.
-- Context Appropriate: POU technologies are considered context-appropriate when the materials to make / maintain / use the technology are locally available and the technology can be reasonable used within the local environment. For example, solar disinfection is only appropriate for contexts where high levels of solar radiation occur on a reliable basis.

indicators.ind: L1- Number of water collection points (taps, faucets, or dispensers) completed as parts of water supply systems in communities

itt.stmt: Community members have access to improved source of drinking water and treat water before consumption
itt.ind: L1- Number of water collection points (taps, faucets, or dispensers) completed as parts of water supply systems in communities
itt.defn:
Number of new water collection points (taps, faucets, or water dispensers) completed as parts (distribution points) of water supply systems in communities as a result of World Vision programming during the reporting period. Water supply systems are defined as: mechanized and solar pumping systems, protected spring systems, piped water systems, and rainwater harvesting systems. Water collection points are "completed" after water quality has been tested in accordance with the World Vision Water Quality Protocol (Diarra, 2021) and certified compliant with World Health Organization (WHO) standards as well as national government standards (where applicable). Water supply systems may NOT begin public service until such testing demonstrates that water quality parameters fall within the acceptable ranges/limits defined by the WHO and national government.


The taps, faucets, and dispensers counted under this indicator represent "improved" water collection points when connected to systems or sources that, by nature their construction and/or through active intervention, have the potential to deliver safe drinking water to the public. The following water supplies are considered as "improved" drinking water facilities: piped drinking water supply on premises; public taps/stand posts; protected spring systems; and rainwater collection systems. Please note that a single tap-stand or point of service may have multiple taps/faucets counted under this indicator. For example, a tap-stand with three (3) separate taps should be counted as 3 units under this indicator.

itt.defn:
This indicator measures number and proportion of child protection cases that have been followed up by child protection (CP) Partner Groups out of total number of child protection cases reported and referred to CP Partner Groups.

"Followed up" refers to action taken to respond to a report of a child protection incident, ensuring do no harm and the best interest of the child.

CP Partner Group is a state entity with a legal mandate to respond to child protection incidents. Depending on the context, CP Partner Groups can have different names. Depending on the context, action taken by CP Partner Groups can include all or either of the following - direct responding and closing the case, referring to specialized services, and follow up with an ongoing case. This indicator measures the ability of the CP Partner Group to follow-up on child protection incidents that have been reported. This indicator should measure all cases reported or referred and followed-up by CP Partner Group regardless of WV direct or indirect contribution to the case report, referral or follow up.

indicators.ind: L1- Prevalence of underweight in children under five years of age

itt.stmt: Improved access to health and nutrition services and positive behaviour change among pregnant women and caregivers of children under five years.
itt.ind: L1- Prevalence of underweight in children under five years of age
itt.defn:
This indicator tracks percent of children aged 0-59 months whose weight for age is less than minus two standard deviations from the median (WAZ) for the international reference population ages 0–59 months.

Underweight is recommended to assess changes in the magnitude of malnutrition over time. It is a composite indicator reflecting both long-term and/or acute short-term malnutrition. Body weight may be lost from malnutrition for a long time and when this happens a child is then low weight-for-age. Weight may also be lost from acute, short-term malnutrition (thinness or wasting), also resulting in a child who is low weight-for-age. Child malnutrition, as reflected in body weight, is selected as an indicator for several reasons. Child underweight is associated to poverty, low levels of education, and poor access to health services. Malnutrition in children, even at moderate levels, increases their risk of death, is associated with poorer cognitive development, and affects health status later in life.

**This indicator is measured under Annual Impact Measurement (AIM)**

This indicator measures EBF in the previous 24 hours for infants 0-5 months of age who are currently living. This indicator is based upon "completed months". For example, the current international standard for exclusive breastfeeding is the provision of breast milk only until 6 months of age. The exclusive breastfeeding indicator therefore includes children aged 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 completed months. This is a proxy indicator because we assume that behaviour during the day prior to interview is representative of a general pattern. This temporal restriction helps minimise problems with recall.To assess EBF, we use a series of questions to accurately obtain information on supplemental foods provided to infants (from DHS). Please note that breast milk includes breast milk that the mother has expressed or breast milk from a wet nurse. Report of giving the child any other liquid or food besides breast milk means EBF does not exist. The only exceptions are when the infant is given ORS, drops, syrups (vitamins, minerals, medicines).

indicators.ind: L1- Proportion of under 5 (U5) with diarrhoea who received effective treatment of diarrhea
indicators.mov: CV004 - Caregiver Survey report,CV028 - LQAS record

itt.stmt: Improved access to health and nutrition services and positive behaviour change among pregnant women and caregivers of children under five years.
itt.ind: L1- Proportion of under 5 (U5) with diarrhoea who received effective treatment of diarrhea
itt.defn:
Percent of parents or caregivers of children aged 0–59 months with diarrhoea in the past two weeks who report that the child received low-osmolarity oral rehydration salts (ORS), zinc and increased breastfeeding and/or fluids and/or continued foods, as appropriate

This indicator measures the prevalence of appropriate management with ORT (oral rehydration therapy) of children age 0-59 months with diarrhoea in the past two weeks. The indicator will be used to measure effectiveness of WV 7-11 health programming. Diarrhoea is defined as more than three loose stools passed during a 24-hour period. ORT prevents and/or corrects the dehydration that is a result of diarrhoea. ORT is a general term that includes: age appropriate continued feeding and increased liquids, plus ORS and zinc supplement. Highly effective treatment defines ORT as increased liquid and continued food plus low osmolarity ORS and zinc. Treatment using low osmolarity ORS and zinc is recommended by the WHO. Only fluid made from an ORS packet solution, a sachet or packet mixed with clean water in the home, and pre-packaged ORS fluid are counted as ORS for this indicator. Please note that home preparations, even if government recommended, are not considered ORS.Continued feeding and increased fluids or breastfeeding during illnesses is necessary to compensate for nutritional losses associated with the illness. For this indicator, infants less than 6 months of age who were given fluids, other than ORS or breast milk, or who were given foods during the illness would be categorised as NOT receiving appropriate treatment.

**This indicator is measured under Annual Impact Measurement (AIM)**

itt.defn:
This indicator measures the percentage of women, ages 15-49, who are married or in union and desire either to have no additional children or to postpone the next child and who are currently using a modern contraceptive method. Women using a traditional method are assumed to have an unmet need for modern contraception. The indicator is also referred to as the demand for family planning satisfied with modern methods. Modern methods of contraception include: female and male sterilization, the intrauterine device (IUD), the implant, injectables, oral contraceptive pills, male and female condoms, vaginal barrier methods (including the diaphragm, cervical cap, and spermicidal foam, jelly, cream, and sponge), the lactational amenorrhoea method (LAM), emergency contraception, and other modern methods not reported separately (e.g., the contraceptive patch or vaginal ring). For the lactational amenorrhoea method (LAM) to be considered a modern method, 3 conditions must be met: 1. Baby is under 6 months 2. Mother is still breastfeeding 3. Menses have not returned.

itt.stmt: Parents, caregivers, and community members provided positive caring and protective relationships to children and adolescents
itt.ind: L1- Proportion of boys and girls (12-18 years) with positive and peaceful relations with their Parent(s)/Caregiver(s)
itt.defn:
This indicator assesses the proportion of boys and girls (aged 12-18) who report having positive and peaceful relationships with their parent(s) or caregiver(s). It focuses on key aspects such as the respect for feelings, understanding, and trust within the family context. It aims to capture the quality of the emotional connection, understanding, trust, and communication within the family unit.

Positive and Peaceful Relationships in Families: Refers to the overall emotional well-being and harmonious interactions between adolescents and their Parent(s)/Caregiver(s), encompassing respect, understanding, trust, shared perspectives, and open communication.

Understanding: Emphasize that this term involves the Parent(s)/Caregiver(s) comprehending the adolescent's feelings and perspectives.

The unit of measurement is the proportion of boys and girls aged 12-18 with positive and peaceful relationships with their parent(s) or caregiver(s). Responses to individual questions (FD13 to FD18) are coded on a scale from 0 to 4, with 0 indicating "Almost Never True" and 4 indicating "Almost Always True."

The indicator relies on self-reported perceptions, which may be influenced by the individual's interpretation and subjectivity.
Cultural norms and expectations may influence the interpretation of positive and peaceful relationships, impacting cross-cultural comparisons.

**This indicator is measured under Annual Impact Measurement (AIM)**

itt.ind: L1- Proportion of adolescents who report having experienced any physical violence and/or psychological aggression by parent/caregivers in the past 12 months
itt.defn:
This is a Child Protection prevalence indicator that measures percent of adolescents aged 12–18 years who report having experienced any physical violence and/or psychological aggression by caregivers in the past 12 months disaggregated by sex. This indicator is aligned with INSPIRE indicator 1.1 and contributes to SDG 16.2.1. It is adapted from VACS physical and emotional violence questions.
Physical violence is defined as the intentional use of physical force with the potential to cause death, disability, injury or harm. Physical violence refers to any of the following actions: slapping, pushing, shoving, shaking, or intentionally throwing something at the participant to cause harm; punching, kicking, whipping, or beating the participant with an object; strangling, smothering, attempting to drown, or intentionally burning the participant; using or threatening the participant with a knife, gun, or any other weapon.
Psychological aggression/emotional violence is defined as a pattern of verbal behaviour over time or an isolated incident that is not developmentally appropriate or supportive and that has a high probability of damaging an adolescent’s mental health or his/her physical, mental, spiritual, moral, or social development. Psychological aggression includes the following behaviors: informing the participant that they were unloved or undeserving of love; telling the participant that someone wished they had never been born or was dead; and subjecting the participant to ridicule or derogatory remarks, such as being called stupid, useless, good for nothing, or big-headed
Caregiver refers to father, mother, step father, step mother, brother, sister or another caregiver.  
Self-administration is highly recommended, please refer to the Ethics Reference Guide to ensure your FO is adhering to Safeguarding policy and ethical protocols

**This indicator is measured under Annual Impact Measurement (AIM)**

indicators.ind: L1- Proportion of adolescents who have a strong connection with their parent or caregiver

itt.stmt: Parents, caregivers, and community members provided positive caring and protective relationships to children and adolescents
itt.ind: L1- Proportion of adolescents who have a strong connection with their parent or caregiver
itt.defn:
This indicator measures the percentage of adolescents aged 12-18 years who feel strongly connected with their parents and/or primary caregivers. This is one of the key aspects of the environment in which adolescents live. Strong connection is measured in terms of the closeness of relationships between adolescents and parents or primary caregivers. Relationship with their primary caregivers is a major influencing factor on children’s well-being and their ability to develop and thrive. The items for measuring connection have been tested and validated in 12 different cultural settings. The 15 statements that comprise the connection indicator are about the young person’s relationship with parents or primary caregivers. The respondents are asked to choose from a list of adults, for example, mother, father, grandparent, aunt/uncle and guardian, the one with whom they spend most time. Adolescents who perceive that their caregivers support them in the ways measured in this indicator have statistically higher levels of well-being and lower levels of risk behaviours.

**This indicator is measured under Annual Impact Measurement (AIM)**

Psychological aggression includes acts such as yelling, screaming or calling the child names.

itt.stmt: Children and adolescents have improved life skills and resilience to protect themselves and participate in decision making
itt.ind: L1- Proportion of boys and girls (12-18 years) with positive and peaceful relations with their peers
itt.defn:
This indicator assesses the proportion of boys and girls (aged 12-18) who report having positive and peaceful relationships with their peers. It aims to capture the quality of emotional connections, understanding, trust, mutual perspectives, and care within the peer group.

Positive and Peaceful Relationships with Peers: Encompasses the overall well-being and harmonious interactions between adolescents and their friends, including respect, understanding, trust, shared perspectives, and genuine care.

Understanding: Emphasize that this term involves friends comprehending the adolescent's feelings and perspectives.

The unit of measurement is the proportion of boys and girls aged 12-18 with positive and peaceful relationships with their peers. Responses to individual questions (FD19 to FD24) are coded on a scale from 0 to 4, with 0 indicating "Almost Never True" and 4 indicating "Almost Always True."

Dynamic Nature of Peer Relationships: Peer dynamics can change over time, and responses may reflect the current state rather than the long-term stability of relationships.

itt.defn:
This indicator measures number of children aged 6-11 years and adolescents aged 12-18 years who meaningfully participated in actions that support ending violence against children.

Actions can include various activities that support ending violence against children. Examples include involvement in community projects against violence against children (VAC), engagement in meetings with local community leaders to address issues related to ending violence against children (EVAC), participation in social accountability gatherings to enhance the quality of child protection services, and involvement in child-led research focused on EVAC.

Meaningful participation means that the engagement of children and adolescents is relevant, informed, consented, child-friendly, safe and sensitive to diversity. Children and adolescents are not only consulted but they are part of the decision-making. This implies that they are not only ‘taking part’ but they are participating in the design, implementation, and monitoring of the actions.

itt.stmt: Target communities led climate change mitigation intervention for well-being of their children
itt.ind: # of people who participated in the development, adoption and/or implementation of local disaster risk reduction strategies or climate change plans
itt.defn:
Number of people who participated in the development, adoption and/or implementation of local disaster risk reduction strategies or climate change plans associated with project activities. A Disaster risk reduction (DRR) strategy outlines actions for reducing local hazard-related disaster risks and sets the strategic direction for the community to become more resilient to disasters. DRR strategies should define goals and objectives across different timescales and included concrete targets, indicators and timeframes.  A climate change plan outlines the mitigation and adaptation activities that the community intend to take to help reduce their contribution to climate change and enhance their resilience to the impacts of climate change.

*** Cambodia context, we will measure on number of people  who participated in the development, adoption and/or implementation climate change mitigation plan including tree plantation, solar use at home/public, use of efficient cook stove, waste management compaign, etc.
